summary: This Dockerfile builds a lightweight Alpine Linux image with Docker installed, then creates a non-root user account with a home directory and proper permissions. The user ID, group ID, and username are configurable through build arguments so the image can be customized at build time.

explanations.5: ARG lets you pass values when building the image (docker build --build-arg DOCKER_OS_GROUPID=1000), providing defaults here if not specified.
explanations.15: These ARG lines re-declare the same variables after the FROM statement so they're available in this stage; Docker build arguments don't automatically carry through FROM unless redeclared.
explanations.19: set -e -x makes the RUN command exit on any error (e) and print each command before running (x), so you see exactly what failed if something goes wrong.
explanations.21: addgroup creates a Linux group (like a team) with a specific numeric ID that users can belong to; this one is for our application user.
explanations.23: adduser creates the actual user account; the flags mean: -S (system user), -D (no password), -u (user ID), -G (primary group), -h (home directory path), and the last argument is the username.
explanations.27: USER switches the container to run as this non-root user instead of root, which is a security best practice—containers run as this account by default now.
